items.headline: RNA medicine enters its second act
items.preview: The COVID-19 pandemic has accelerated the development of RNA therapeutics, expanding their applications.
items.article:
The COVID-19 pandemic transformed RNA technologies into one of the most visible scientific breakthroughs of the decade. mRNA vaccines demonstrated unprecedented speed of development, large-scale manufacturing capability, and global deployment, pushing RNA therapeutics into the public spotlight. But according to companies working in the field, the pandemic was not the beginning of the RNA story. Instead, it accelerated technologies that had already been under development for years.
Why this matters: Today, the field is rapidly evolving beyond vaccines into oncology, cardiovascular medicine, autoimmune disease, and gene regulation, with RNA being viewed as a programmable therapeutic platform.
One of the central themes emerging across the RNA field is that RNA therapeutics encompasses multiple fundamentally different modalities. This diversity allows developers to approach RNA as a flexible engineering platform capable of encoding multiple biological functions, which is changing how companies think about therapeutic development.

items.headline: How Can Stem Cell Therapy Help Multiple Sclerosis Patients in Mexico?
items.preview: Stem cell therapy offers a promising approach for MS patients in Mexico, focusing on immune modulation.
items.article:
Stem cell therapy can significantly help Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients in Mexico by modulating the immune system to cease its attack on the nervous system. This innovative approach promotes the repair of damaged myelin sheaths, potentially restoring lost function and improving quality of life. Patients can often achieve these outcomes at a cost significantly lower than in the US or Europe, with treatments ranging from $8,000 to $25,000 USD in COFEPRIS-regulated facilities.
Why this matters: This regenerative medical approach aims to reset the immune system and repair neural damage, offering hope for patients who have limited relief from conventional therapies.
Key benefits include immune system modulation, myelin repair, and symptom improvement, making stem cell therapy a viable option for many MS patients seeking effective treatment.

items.headline: Where Can Parkinson’s Disease Patients Access Stem Cell Therapy in Mexico?
items.preview: Patients with Parkinson's disease can find affordable stem cell therapy options in Mexico.
items.article:
Parkinson’s disease patients can access specialized stem cell therapy at top-rated clinics across Mexico, including MexStemCells Clinic in Mexico City and Stem Solutions in Monterrey. These facilities offer comprehensive packages ranging from $4,000 to $8,500 USD, providing a significantly more affordable alternative compared to costs exceeding $20,000 in the US or Europe.
Why this matters: Stem cell therapy has emerged as a promising approach to address the underlying neurodegeneration in Parkinson’s disease, potentially improving motor function and quality of life.
The treatment typically involves mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and aims to reduce neuroinflammation while promoting the regeneration of dopamine-producing neurons, offering hope for patients seeking innovative therapies.

items.headline: 2026 catalysts: First-half scorecard
items.preview: The first half of 2026 saw significant progress in RNA modalities and cardiorenal programs.
items.article:
The first half of 2026 brought encouraging clinical data and positive regulatory decisions across new modalities and cardiorenal programs. Most of the major catalysts flagged by BioCentury met expectations, although antisense performance was mixed and the period’s most anticipated RNA readout was delayed.
Why this matters: This period is pivotal for RNA modalities, with notable breakthroughs and challenges shaping the competitive landscape, particularly for antisense oligonucleotides.
Despite mixed results in some areas, the advancements in RNA technologies signal a promising future for therapeutic development.

items.headline: Noise-invariant representations of sound emerge along the canonical cortical hierarchy
items.preview: Research reveals how neurons in the auditory system achieve noise-invariant sound representation.
items.article:
Neurons in the auditory system must represent behaviorally relevant sounds in the presence of background noise to support noise-invariant perception and behavior. This study examines how excitatory subpopulations within the auditory cortex contribute to this transformation from noise-dependent to noise-invariant coding.
Why this matters: Understanding the mechanisms of noise-invariant coding can enhance our knowledge of auditory processing and inform future research in auditory neuroscience.
The findings reveal a functional division of labor in the auditory cortex, with deep-layer pathways preferentially carrying noise-invariant representations, suggesting distinct roles for different excitatory neuron populations.
